citation.title: Multimodal Machine Learning: A Survey and Taxonomy
citation.authors: Tadas Baltrusaitis; Chaitanya Ahuja; Louis-Philippe Morency
citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

topic: Generic survey and taxonomy of multimodal machine learning: representation, translation, alignment, fusion and co-learning.
own_question: How can recent multimodal machine learning work be organized into common technical challenges beyond the early-versus-late fusion split?
actual_method_and_evidence: Literature survey. It presents no new experiments and no fusion-plasma content. Its taxonomy is the authors' organizing interpretation, not a demonstrated result.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Multimodal fusion approaches are commonly grouped as early (feature-level), late (decision-level) and hybrid, alongside model-based approaches.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a general ML categorization. It does not establish that BES/ECEI information adds value for predicting CES reports.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. There is no plasma diagnostic, causal timing or nowcasting content.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim the source supports causal nowcasting of CES reports.
Do not infer that fusing BES/ECEI improves CES temperature estimates.
Do not treat the taxonomy as proof that any physics mechanism exists.
Do not use it to characterize plasma prior work.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most it could serve as an optional background citation for early/late fusion terminology when describing how BES/ECEI inputs are combined with past CES reports. It is not needed for the paper's framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
